stage_messages.history: Good questions uncover the mechanism and red flags. You do not need to ask everything—ask what changes your decisions.

stage_messages.diagnosis: Now connect the mechanism, examination and investigations. Which diagnosis actually explains all three?

stage_messages.knowledge_check: Nice work! Three quick questions to lock in the clinical reasoning.
stage_messages.completion: Great job with Sofia! The best clinicians are careful about both decisions and patient safety.

case_specific_guidance.diagnostic_nudge: What direction did the arm move, and what happened to the shoulder contour?
case_specific_guidance.differentiating_clue: Anterior dislocations follow abduction/external rotation and show an anteroinferior humeral head.
case_specific_guidance.clinical_coaching: Examine axillary nerve and perfusion, review trauma X-rays, arrange qualified gentle reduction, recheck nerves and confirm with post-reduction films.
critical_red_flags: Associated proximal humerus or glenoid fracture
key_teaching_points: Document axillary nerve before and after reduction.
First-time traumatic dislocation needs radiographic confirmation.
Gentle monitored reduction and post-reduction imaging are key.
Early rehab and recurrence-risk counseling are important in young patients.

history.message: Focus on the injury mechanism, neurovascular symptoms, wounds and other associated injuries. Traumatic abduction/external rotation with immediate shoulder displacement.

examination.message: Start with these case-specific findings: Axillary nerve sensation over lateral deltoid intact. Radial pulse present, warm hand. Red flag: Absent distal perfusion.

investigations.message: Select investigations that will change management. Initial priority: Right shoulder trauma radiographs: AP and scapular-Y/axillary-equivalent view. What direction did the arm move, and what happened to the shoulder contour?

diagnosis.message: Anterior dislocations follow abduction/external rotation and show an anteroinferior humeral head.

treatment.message: Examine axillary nerve and perfusion, review trauma X-rays, arrange qualified gentle reduction, recheck nerves and confirm with post-reduction films.
